Nested Component Hierarchy from Spec

The file `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\flat_scene.dae` contains a flat list of 20 COLLADA `<node>` elements directly under the visual scene root. Each node carries a full world-space transform (any combination of translation and rotation) and references one of the geometry definitions in `library_geometries`.

The file `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\hierarchy.json` specifies how these 20 flat instances must be reorganized into a nested group hierarchy, using exactly this schema:

```
{
"groups": [
{"name": "<GroupName>", "children": ["<NodeName>",...]},...
]
}
```

There are exactly 4 groups. Every one of the 20 flat node names appears in exactly one group's `children` list (the 4 groups partition the 20 nodes, 5 each).

1. Parse `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\flat_scene.dae` and record the world-space transform of every named node.
2. Parse `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\hierarchy.json`.
3. Emit `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\answer.skp` whose visual scene graph has exactly 4 top-level `<node>` elements - one per group - each named as specified by `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\hierarchy.json`. Each group node contains as its direct children the `<node>` elements listed in `children` (keep the original child names). Group nodes may carry their own transform; child nodes carry whatever local transform is needed so that the cumulative parent*child transform reproduces the original flat-scene world transform within 1 mm.
4. Geometry definitions must not be duplicated - reuse the same `<geometry>` ids from the input file.

Requirements:
1. `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\answer.skp` can be opened and inspected as a native SketchUp model.
2. The scene graph has exactly 4 top-level nodes with the 4 group names from `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\hierarchy.json`.
3. Each group node contains exactly the child node names specified, with no extras and no duplicates.
4. Node tree depth is at least 2 (groups contain nested children, not direct geometry).
5. For every one of the 20 instances, the recovered world transform (group_matrix * child_matrix applied to the local geometry origin (0,0,0)) matches the original flat-scene world position within 1 mm.
6. All 20 child nodes still reference their original geometry definition.
